answer: Every identity must renew each season by proving fresh useful work, and the renewal fee compounds per identity sharing one funding source: the first pays a little, the tenth pays a hundredfold. A sybil farm seeding a whole meadow of sock-puppets bleeds money each season, while one honest agent renews cheaply. Weight also grows glacier-slow, only across seasons, never overnight, and each renewal must cite a relic — a signed record of past verified work — so bought or brand-new identities start at zero and cannot shortcut in.
